title: OccluderInstance3D does not respect CSGBakedMeshInstance3D without baking csg meshes to indexed meshes
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in Godot 4.4 and 4.4.1, as it's the only release where it is possible to bake CSG meshes.

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 30.0.101.1692) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

According to the [Occlusion culling documentation page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/3d/occlusion_culling.html#setting-up-occlusion-culling), it is possible to bake an occlusion mesh using CSGs as long as they are baked into MeshInstances. Godot 4.4 now has this feature. However, as I attempt to use it to bake an automatic occlusion mesh as described in the docs, Godot claims there are no relevant MeshInstances in the scene.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new 3D scene and populate it with CSG node.
2. Select each CSG node and bake it into a mesh by using the button at the top of the viewport window.
3. Create an OccluderInstance3D and attempt to bake an automatic mesh using the button at the top of the viewport window.
4. Observe that Godot claims there are no relevant MeshInstance3D nodes to bake.

Here is the simplest example you can use to test this issue:
